learning_outcomes.text: Acquire fundamental knowledge in materials science, specifically: Know the main materials used in Mechanical Engineering, their main properties (thermal and mechanical) and applications.
Understand and relate the various factors that contribute to the great diversity of mechanical behaviour of materials (structure, chemical composition, defects, chemical bonds, processing).
Understand the basic principles of fracture mechanics, fatigue and creep (fluence).
Know the main mechanical tests (tensile, hardness, toughness, fatigue, creep) to determine the mechanical properties of materials.
Understand the main forms of materials degradation and processes to minimize or avoid them.
Perform experimental work related to the contents of the course unit.
Develop transversal competencies in extracurricular teamwork and report writing.
Understand in an integrated, deep and diverse way the material issues - structure, properties, processing and performance - that are fundamental to produce everything we use and need.
Be aware of the great diversity of factors that are fundamental in material selection.

syllabus_topics: MATERIAL DEGRADATION: Electrochemical concepts. Corrosion and forms of corrosion. Main methods of materials protection.
CHEMICAL BONDS AND STRUCTURES: Atom structure. Chemical bonds. Crystalline and amorphous structures. X-ray diffraction.
PHASE DIAGRAMS: Diffusion. Phases. Binary diagrams: rules of interpretation, cooling curves. Ternary diagrams.

MECHANICAL BEHAVIOR: Tension and extension. Elastic and plastic behavior. Hooke's law and elastic properties. Tensile test and engineering curve. Strength and ductility. Theoretical resistance of crystals. Defects in metallic materials. Plastic deformation of monocrystals and polycrystals. Hardening mechanisms. Recrystallization.
THERMAL PROPERTIES: Heat capacity. Thermal expansion. Thermal conductivity. Thermal stresses.
FLUENCE: Fluence mechanical behavior. Tests, curves, mechanisms.
FATIGUE AND FRACTURE: Fragile and ductile fracture. Toughness. Fatigue behavior of materials.
teaching_methods: Theoretical-practical classes (presentation of theoretical concepts, practical exercises solved by teacher, suggested exercises for autonomous solution)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated from two partial tests (45% each, with a minimum of 6 points in each) and experimental activities (10%, as an average of two reports). To obtain attendance, students must comply with FEUP's regulations on attendance and score at least 6 points in one of the written tests. If experimental activities are not performed, exams count for 100% of the final grade. Approved students can improve their grade for part 1, part 2, or the overall score in a resource exam, with the best classification being counted, but experimental activity grades cannot be improved.
